result.title: PsycheMME: A Psychology-Informed Benchmark for Social Understanding and Interaction in Videos
result.summary: Understanding human needs and selecting responses require distinct judgments that aggregate accuracy can obscure. We introduce PsycheMME, a video benchmark informed by psychology, with eight capabilities spanning grounding, states, needs, interaction decisions, memory, and risk. Drawing on Social Information Processing and the Perception-Action Cycle, this organization separates human understanding from response selection. We construct 1,000 questions from 630 episodes through independent answering with proposed references withheld and expert review. Our Reasoning-Verified protocol weights answer credit by the support and logical consistency of explicit rationales against annotated cues. Across 17 models, Timing has the lowest Verified scores and credit retention, with weaker support judgments for correct Timing answers. Models with similar Need scores still differ in answer completeness on open questions. Input controls and SFT/GRPO examine context dependence and adaptation. Evaluating answers alongside rationales locates where models fail across understanding, response selection, and justification.

AI.brief_summary: PsycheMME 构建心理学启发的视频社会理解基准：从 630 段视频经独立作答与专家复核生成 1000 道题，覆盖 grounding、心理状态、需求、交互决策、记忆与风险八类能力，并提出按显式理由对标注线索的支持度与逻辑一致性加权的 Reasoning-Verified 评分，用于评测 17 个模型及 SFT/GRPO 适配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「理由是否被标注视觉线索支持」的核查式评分可能可供核查 LVR 中答案对视觉证据的实际依赖与贡献分配评估，但任务限于社会性视频理解，迁移性尚待判断。
